disagreement_resolution.rule: reviewer disagreement in either direction becomes uncertain

resolved.reviewer_note: The rule admits a mixed cohort only if 'a separately identifiable disease cohort receives the labeled intervention AND its clinical outcomes are separately specified'. I agree the AD cohort is separately identifiable (dedicated 'Mild Alzheimer's Disease (AD) MB' and 'AD Placebo' arms) and that the methylene-blue contrast is separable from the constant phenazopyridine. I read the second conjunct more strictly: the outcomesModule registers one undifferentiated set of measures across all eight arms, and no registered outcome is specified for the AD cohort. The adjudicator supplies the separation from a detailedDescription hypothesis ('effects on memory will be greater in the MCI and mild AD groups than in the healthy aging group'), which is an analysis-plan statement rather than a separately specified outcome. The AD-group inclusion text, 'Alzheimer's Early-stage, sporadic-type', also cites no diagnostic criteria. Under 'Missing evidence fails closed' I land on uncertain. This is a close call and the adjudicator's reading is defensible.

The adjudicator excludes on no_clinical_objective, citing the briefSummary line 'The primary endpoint will be change in cerebral glucose metabolism', and describes MoCA as 'an exploratory secondary measure'. The same briefSummary opens 'This single-center, uncontrolled pilot study aims to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of six months of intermittently dosed oral rapamycin (sirolimus) in subjects with early-stage Alzheimer's disease', and 'Change in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) rating' is registered under outcomesModule.secondaryOutcomes, not otherOutcomes. The rule says clinical secondary outcomes count when the objective explicitly studies the drug's clinical effects; a stated efficacy objective in diagnosed AD plus a registered cognitive secondary outcome meets that. This is also the structure the adjudicator accepted for 14218:NCT04552795:3tc (non-clinical primaries, 'efficacy' in the objective, a cognitive secondary outcome), so I read the two records as requiring the same outcome.

The adjudicator includes, resting the clinical limb on briefSummary 'and cognitive performance.' plus 'ADAS-Cog 14' at outcomesModule.otherOutcomes.19. Both quotes are accurate. I read the rule's clause as reaching only clinical secondary outcomes ('Clinical secondary outcomes count if the objective explicitly studies the drug's clinical effects'); here every clinical measure sits in exploratory other outcomes, the single primary outcome is an MR-spectroscopy proxy, and the detailedDescription states 'The primary objective of the study is to assess the effect of 12 weeks of 10mg dapagliflozin once daily on cerebral NAA'. With the objective's cognitive language framed as 'explore' and no clinical primary or secondary outcome, I treat the affirmative Gate 3 evidence as incomplete and fail closed to uncertain rather than include.

The adjudicator excludes, holding that 'The broad secondary cognitive/functional measure is not explicitly tied to a clinical-effect objective'. The registered secondary outcome's own description states the objective in terms: 'Determine comparative efficacy of perindopril vs. telmisartan on cognitive and functional measures and on other structural brain imaging'. That is an explicit clinical-effect objective, registered, and attached to a secondary (not exploratory) clinical outcome, which is exactly what the rule's clinical-secondary clause requires. I also note the asymmetry with 15201:NCT03801642:dapagliflozin, which the adjudicator included on weaker clinical-limb evidence (an 'explore' phrase plus an exploratory other outcome); telmisartan's clinical-objective evidence is at least as strong.

I reach the same practical effect (not a positive) but a different label, and the stated ground differs. The adjudicator's rationale asserts 'the registered endpoints are adverse events, PK and pharmacodynamics, with no clinical symptom/function/cognition effect'; the record does register clinical measures, namely 'Change in Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-cognitive scale', 'Change in Mini Mental State Examination', 'Change in Alzheimer's disease Clinical Activities of Daily Living Scale' and 'Change in Clinical Dementia Rating Scale (CDR-SB)' under outcomesModule.otherOutcomes, and the detailedDescription says the study 'will test the effects of Salsalate on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteins, brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and cognitive (thinking and memory) tests'. Because those clinical measures are exploratory rather than primary or secondary, I treat the Gate 3 evidence as incomplete rather than absent, which under the rule is uncertain, not exclude. Either way the record is not a positive.
